summary: The main article describes a photoinduced Co/Ni-cocatalyzed Markovnikov hydroarylation of unactivated olefins using aryl bromides and protons as a hydrogen source. The document includes optimization tables, reaction scopes for both olefins and aryl bromides, and mechanistic studies including radical trapping and deuterium labeling.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Transition-metal-catalyzed hydroarylation of unactivated alkenes and photoinduced MHAT reaction.
items.description: This scheme compares previous methods for hydroarylation using Co/Ni or Fe/Ni systems with hydrosilanes to the current photoinduced Co/Ni-cocatalyzed approach using protons.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions a
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of catalysts, photocatalysts, solvents, and control experiments to determine the optimal conditions for the hydroarylation of 1a and 2a.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Scope of olefins.
items.description: This scheme illustrates the variety of terminal and internal alkenes that are compatible with the reaction, including functional group tolerance and gram-scale synthesis.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Scope of aryl bromides.
items.description: This scheme displays the electronic and steric diversity of aryl bromides and heteroaryl bromides that can be used in the hydroarylation process.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Mechanistic study experiments.
items.description: This scheme details radical scavenging, ring-closure, and deuterium labeling experiments used to probe the reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Proposed mechanism.
items.description: A proposed catalytic cycle involving photoinduced electron transfer, Co-mediated MHAT, and Ni-catalyzed cross-coupling.
